segments.text: Matthew Henry begins with wonder: the holy God loves a wicked world.
Chrysostom measures that love by what the Father gave: his Son, for ungrateful slaves.
The next verse says why the Son was sent. Augustine pictures a physician who has come to heal the sick.
Matthew Henry turns to the one who believes: he is not condemned, and that is more than a reprieve.

study.title: The Love That Gives (narrative, selected sentences)
study.focus: What does God's gift of his Son tell us about the heart of God?
study.take: This is Study E's plan told as one story. Scripture and the teachers' words are printed exactly; the short bridges between them are the AI's and are marked.
study.question: Christ came to heal, not to condemn. What does believing in him look like for you this week?
study.closing: The passages in this study point the same way: the Son was given to rescue, and the one who believes is not condemned. The gift is already offered; believing is how it is received.

scripture.16: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
scripture.17: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.
scripture.18: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God.

labels.jewish_source: A later Jewish writing that Gill cites; not a statement of what people believed in Jesus's day.
